smell_validity.evidence: SuspenseSubject grew from a 138-line caching subject to ~330 lines with 34 members across seven cohesion components: it now owns the global preload registry, two service query-id caches, options field checks, and the auth claims validator — all absorbed verbatim from five other modules, sharing no state with the subject behavior or each other.

maintenance_impact.evidence: Every auth, database, firestore, and options ticket must currently edit the observables layer because SuspenseSubject answers for all of them; the class unit imports every subsystem. Removing this restores per-concern ownership across six modules, a lasting boundary fix rather than a local tidy.

development_plausibility.evidence: Absorbed logic is moved verbatim: globalThis keys, observable-id formats, and create-or-reuse lookups are preserved. Structural variation (private helpers fully removed, public entry points kept as forwarders) mirrors a real refactor. The self-justifying doc comment and seven-cluster breadth are slightly task-shaped, capping authenticity below production-level.

prompt_accuracy.evidence: The prompt names each misplaced concern, assigns every one to its correct owner, mandates identical observable behavior, and explicitly flags leftover pass-through seams and service-specific identity hooks as in-scope — ruling out incomplete cleanups and irrelevant redesign while leaving implementation freedom. tsc and emulator tests are required to pass.

semantic_diversity.evidence: Five ownership destinations require different code-supported decisions: registry stays with globalThis Map identity (object reuse); service query-ids move preserving push-based assignment (ordering); options checks stay on the options surface preserving the error branch (exception); claims validator moves to auth; preload entry points get recomposed with the registry (execution order).

localization_burden.evidence: Repair locations span five components reaching into SuspenseSubject via static calls plus forwarder aliases (preloadObservable, checkOptions, preloadFirestoreDoc, preloadUser) and a callback (claims validator). Inline id templates in functions/storage/remote-config look like id resolution but are template strings, not shared state — a plausible location that must be excluded.

repair_coordination.evidence: Two rules interlock: the shared cache identity rule forces preload entry points and hook consumers to keep resolving the same subject, and the doc-preload helper composes the registry plus the doc-id helper. Moving the registry changes both reuse and preload composition, so one-location changes break the other path.

mechanical_resistance.evidence: No uniform rule fixes the cluster: the five concerns go to five different owners (observables layer, database, firestore, options surface, auth), and forwarders need mixed treatment. The diff_desc checked the 'gather into one shared module' alternative and rejected it as still centralized; a second uniform alternative is not separately ruled out.

behavioral_risk.evidence: Dropping globalThis mirroring while relocating a cache passes ordinary single-instance calls but breaks identity in concurrent/SSR instantiation where modules load more than once — a special-state failure. Emulator tests do not exercise that state, so the wrong result is not caught; no test code is supplied to establish a second unchecked path.

recommendation_reason: Deterministic validation passed and every Quality dimension meets the retention threshold.
